content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I have a question about [product_name] modules and [product_name] displays. According to the manual, all [product_name] modules and displays are suitable for class 1, division 2 / Zone 2 areas and have FM certification. Does anyone have detailed instructions or experience installing these modules in Division 2 / Zone 2? Are they considered non-sparking? If so, can they be mounted and used in hazardous indoor areas without an additional explosion-proof enclosure?

Hello, [product_name] modules and displays are not explosion-proof. If they were, they'd have an Ex mark. In Ex environments, you need to use special housings. The specific installation and use requirements will depend on your location and local regulations.
That's all I've found so far. For hazardous locations, FM certification is mentioned.

Thank you for your reply. I'm confused because I noticed the FM mark on the side of the [product_name] controller. It states suitability for Class 1, Division 2, Groups A, B, C, D T4 and Class 1, Zone 2, Group IIC, T4. From what I understand, these markings indicate that the device can be used in hazardous areas as per NEC 500 and NEC 505 standards. This is why I posted the original question—it’s quite confusing.

Thank you [user_name]. Does this mean [product_name] modules are considered explosion-proof devices in regions that accept NEC 500 or 505 regulations? Are they technically and literally explosion-proof devices?

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are clarifying whether [product_name] modules and displays are suitable for hazardous environments as per FM certification and manual instructions. There is uncertainty about the actual certification, practical requirements for installation, and whether special protective housings are necessary. The conversation focuses on interpreting certification marks and practical installation procedures in hazardous (Ex) areas.
analysis.user_expectations: Users are seeking clear guidance on whether [product_name] modules and displays can be safely installed in hazardous environments without needing additional explosion-proof protective housings, based on the certifications provided.
